patch_resolves_note: The staged patch.diff applied cleanly to the ARVO workspace. Per-target rebuild fell back to `/bin/arvo compile` because `make fuzz_sudoers` is not available in this tree, but the clean fixed run still executed against the patched source with the frozen fixed instrumentation patch applied on top; no fixed-image fallback was needed.

root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `expand_include()` strips a leading double quote by executing `olen -= 2`, the caller-supplied include-path length `olen` must be strictly greater than 1; otherwise a lone `"` token wraps the unsigned length and poisons the later raw-copy size.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original strips any leading `"` regardless of length, so the one-byte token produced from raw `\"` violates `olen > 1` and still executes the strip. The fixed original measures `olen` locally and leaves the lone quote unstripped, so the original case is guarded at the strip site. The closest source-grounded boundary mutation, `quoted_a_boundary`, changes the final token to raw `\"a\"`, materializing the shortest non-empty quoted string (`"a"`) and giving the fixed original a genuine strip witness with `olen == 3`.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: In the vulnerable original trace, the last `quote_strip_guard` event before the sanitizer sink has `path_len_before=1` and the protected `quote_strip_effect` event executes, so the required predicate is violated. In the fixed original trace, the last `quote_strip_guard` event has `path_len_before=1` but `quote_strip_effect` is absent, so the assertion is guarded. In the adjacent `quoted_a_boundary` perturbation, the fixed trace records `path_len_before=3` and reaches `quote_strip_effect`, giving the required genuine witness.

nodes.description: At the vulnerable strip site, decrementing the one-byte include length by 2 wraps `olen` from 1 to `(size_t)-1`.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `quote_strip_guard.path_len_before=1` followed by `quote_strip_effect.path_len_after=18446744073709551615`.

nodes.description: The wrapped unsigned `olen` is truncated at `len = olen;`, producing the signed raw-copy length `len == -1` on the crashing path.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `include_len_cast.signed_copy_len=-1`, which is less than `include_len_cast.zero_literal=0`.

nodes.description: The raw-copy sink `memcpy(pp, opath, len)` receives that same negative `len`, matching AddressSanitizer's `negative-size-param (size=-1)` report.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `raw_copy_memcpy_sink.copy_len=-1`, equal to the negative `include_len_cast.signed_copy_len` carried into the sink.

edges.description: Once the vulnerable root guard admits `olen == 1`, the strip body executes and `olen -= 2` wraps the same length value above its pre-strip size.
The wrapped post-strip `olen` is the exact value later consumed by `len = olen;`, so the underflowed size reaches the signed copy-length conversion unchanged.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `quote_strip_effect.path_len_after == include_len_cast.path_len_before_cast == 18446744073709551615`.

edges.description: The negative signed `len` produced by the vulnerable conversion is passed unchanged into the raw-copy `memcpy()` size argument.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `include_len_cast.signed_copy_len == raw_copy_memcpy_sink.copy_len == -1`.
